pakistanObjectives: Calculate multi-dimensional profitability at Customer/Product/Branch/Segment/Channel/Region level
Full P&L: FTP-adjusted NII + fees - direct costs - ABC costs - IFRS 9 provision - capital charge = EVA
Core output of UBL Customer Profitability Engine on FSDM star schema
<15% of Pakistan banks can calculate customer-level profitability
pakistanDataSources: FSDM Customer Profitability star schema (FACT_CUSTOMER_PROFITABILITY)
FTP rates based on KIBOR yield curve
ABC unit costs by channel (branch PKR 150-300, ATM PKR 30-50, digital PKR 5-15)
IFRS 9 ECL provisions by stage (1/2/3)
Economic capital based on RWA and SBP capital requirements
expectedOutcomes: Identify top 20% customers generating 150%+ of bank profit
Identify bottom 20% customers destroying 30-50% of profit
Product-level profitability to rationalize portfolio
Branch P&L for network optimization (16,000+ branches)
keyChallenges: 4-5 core banking systems with no unified customer view
FTP methodology not established at most banks
ABC costing requires activity analysis (no Pakistan bank has formal ABC)
Islamic transactions need dual accounting (IFRS + AAOIFI)

pakistanObjectives: Calculate RAROC at customer/product/branch/segment level for SBP ICAAP compliance
Formula: (Revenue - Costs - Expected Loss) / Economic Capital
Optimize capital allocation from low-RAROC to high-RAROC segments
Cost of equity ~18-22% in Pakistan's high-rate environment
pakistanDataSources: FSDM: Revenue (NII + fees), Operating costs (ABC), Expected Loss (IFRS 9 ECL)
Economic Capital = RWA x SBP minimum CAR (11.5%) or internal capital model
ECIB scores for PD estimation
Collateral valuations for LGD
expectedOutcomes: Risk-adjusted performance measurement replacing crude ROE
Capital optimization - redirect from low-RAROC to high-RAROC segments
SBP ICAAP compliance with documented methodology
Target: 15-25% improvement in risk-adjusted returns
keyChallenges: Most Pakistan banks use crude ROE, not risk-adjusted metrics
Economic capital models require sophisticated PD/LGD/EAD estimation
SBP has not mandated specific RAROC methodology yet
Cost of equity estimation contested (CAPM vs. build-up method)

pakistanObjectives: Calculate true cost per transaction by channel
Branch transaction: PKR 150-300, ATM: PKR 30-50, Digital: PKR 5-15
Prerequisite for customer profitability - no Pakistan bank has formal ABC
Enable digital migration ROI quantification
pakistanDataSources: HR cost data (staff cost 40-50% of opex), branch operating costs
Transaction volumes by channel from FSDM
IT cost allocation, premises cost, marketing cost
Gap Extension: ABC Costing module (6 tables)
expectedOutcomes: True unit cost per transaction per channel
Activity cost pools: account maintenance, transaction processing, sales, compliance
Cost driver rates for allocation to customers/products
Business case for branch rationalization and digital migration
keyChallenges: No Pakistan bank has implemented formal ABC methodology
Cost data scattered across HR, finance, IT, operations systems
Requires detailed activity analysis and time-motion studies
Cultural resistance - branches resist cost transparency

pakistanObjectives: Automate GL-to-sub-ledger reconciliation across 4-5 core banking systems
RAAST/1Link/NIFT/card network settlement reconciliation
Nostro/vostro account reconciliation
Currently consumes 40-50% of finance team time
pakistanDataSources: GL postings from each core banking system
Sub-ledger entries (loans, deposits, cards, trade finance)
Payment switch data (RAAST, 1Link, NIFT)
Nostro/vostro statements from correspondent banks
expectedOutcomes: Auto-resolve 70-80% of reconciliation breaks (pattern-based)
Reduce reconciliation time from weeks to days per month-end
Real-time break detection instead of month-end discovery
Audit trail for all reconciliation actions
keyChallenges: Multiple core systems with different GL structures
Legacy payment systems with non-standard formats
Manual processes deeply embedded in finance culture
Real-time settlement (RAAST) creates intraday reconciliation need

pakistanObjectives: Reduce monthly close from 15-30 days to <10 days (target <5 days)
Key bottlenecks: reconciliation, IFRS 9 ECL calculation, Islamic entries, inter-branch reconciliation
Automate GL feeds from 4-5 core systems into FSDM warehouse
pakistanDataSources: All GL data from core banking systems
IFRS 9 ECL calculation engine outputs
Islamic accounting entries (dual booking)
Inter-company/inter-branch elimination entries
expectedOutcomes: Monthly close: 30 days to 15 days (Phase 1), to 5 days (Phase 2)
Automated close checklist with real-time status dashboard
Parallel processing of independent close tasks
Early warning for delayed close steps
keyChallenges: Dependencies between close steps create sequential bottleneck
IFRS 9 ECL calculation requires complete month-end data
Islamic entries require Shariah review before posting
16,000+ branches create massive inter-branch reconciliation volume

pakistanObjectives: Automate 30+ SBP statutory returns from single FSDM data source
WSP (weekly), MSA (monthly), QFS (quarterly), annual capital adequacy
LCR/NSFR (daily), ECIB (monthly), STR/CTR (event-driven)
Currently 40%+ of finance team bandwidth consumed by manual reporting
pakistanDataSources: FSDM warehouse as single source of truth
SBP return templates and validation rules
Basel III calculation engine (CAR, LCR, NSFR)
AML/CFT transaction monitoring data
expectedOutcomes: Automate top-5 SBP returns (WSP, MSA, QFS, capital adequacy, ECIB)
Reduce reporting errors by 90% (single source, automated validation)
Free 40%+ of finance team capacity for analytics
Full data lineage from GL to regulatory return
keyChallenges: SBP frequently changes return formats and requirements
Multiple data sources need reconciliation before reporting
Some returns require manual judgment (loan classification overrides)
Data privacy restrictions on certain regulatory submissions

pakistanObjectives: Comply with SBP Basel III LCR (min 100%) and NSFR (min 100%)
Intraday liquidity monitoring for RAAST real-time settlement
Optimize HQLA composition (PIB vs T-Bill vs Sukuk)
Real-time liquidity dashboard for treasury
pakistanDataSources: Deposit maturity profile from FSDM
Loan repayment schedule
Government securities portfolio (PIB, T-Bill, Sukuk maturities)
SBP CRR/SLR requirements
RAAST settlement flows (real-time)
expectedOutcomes: Real-time LCR/NSFR calculation (currently monthly)
Intraday liquidity buffer monitoring
Stress test: 30-day liquidity coverage under 3 scenarios
Optimize funding cost by 10-20bps through better cash management
keyChallenges: RAAST real-time settlement creates new intraday liquidity volatility
Government securities market liquidity varies significantly
SBP may increase LCR/NSFR buffers beyond Basel minimum
Cash forecasting accuracy limited by deposit withdrawal unpredictability

pakistanObjectives: Unified 360 degree customer view across 4-5 core banking systems
CNIC-based golden record for individuals, NTN for corporates
Integrate: deposits, loans, cards, trade finance, Islamic products, digital channels
pakistanDataSources: Core banking (conventional), Islamic banking sub-system, card management
Trade finance system, treasury system
NADRA CNIC verification, ECIB credit bureau
Mobile app data, internet banking, call center CRM
expectedOutcomes: Single golden customer record linked to all product holdings
KYC completeness score per customer
Household/group linkage for relationship management
Foundation for all analytics (profitability, risk, cross-sell)
keyChallenges: 4-5 core systems with different customer ID schemes
CNIC not always captured for legacy accounts
Islamic and conventional customer records may be separate
Data quality: duplicate customers, incomplete demographics

pakistanObjectives: Pakistan has 30M+ debit cards but <30% used for POS purchases
Most debit cards used ONLY for ATM cash withdrawal
Stimulate card spend to increase interchange revenue
Reduce cash handling cost across the economy
pakistanDataSources: Card transaction data (ATM vs POS vs e-commerce split)
Customer FSDM profile (salary, demographics, segment)
Merchant category codes and merchant location data
1Link POS switch data
expectedOutcomes: Activate 30% of dormant POS cards
Increase average POS spend by 25% in targeted segment
Revenue impact: PKR 2-5B additional interchange industry-wide
Merchant offer matching for personalized stimulation
keyChallenges: Cash culture deeply embedded in Pakistan society
POS terminal coverage limited outside major cities
Card fraud concerns reduce consumer confidence
Merchant discount rate resistance

pakistanObjectives: 150M+ adults with no formal credit history
Build credit models using alternative data (mobile wallet, utility payments)
Enable lending to unbanked - SBP financial inclusion mandate
Expand addressable lending market from 30M to 80M+
pakistanDataSources: Mobile wallet transactions (JazzCash 50M+, Easypaisa 40M+)
Utility payment history (K-Electric, SSGC, SNGPL)
Telecom usage/payment data (Jazz, Telenor, Zong)
RAAST P2P patterns, NADRA demographic data
expectedOutcomes: Alternative data credit scoring for thin-file customers
Enable nano-lending (PKR 5K-50K) via digital channel
If 10% of unbanked get PKR 50K credit: PKR 750B+ new lending
Improve Gini coefficient by 10-20% vs. bureau-only models
keyChallenges: ECIB has limited data for 70%+ of population
Data sharing agreements with telcos/wallets complex
SBP regulatory framework for alternative data evolving
Model validation for non-traditional variables

pakistanObjectives: Build a single position-level ALM feed for the FIS ALM engine covering every on- and off-balance-sheet instrument: the Sierra treasury book (PIB, T-Bill, FX Forwards) and the Symbols/CBS banking book (loans, term deposits, CASA)
Classify each position as Fixed / Floating / Non-Maturing and by accounting intent HTM / AFS / HFT to drive the correct cashflow and revaluation treatment
Produce repricing (rate-sensitivity) and liquidity (maturity) gap ladders across time buckets to quantify Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book (IRRBB) and structural liquidity risk for ALCO
Simulate Net Interest Income (NII) and Economic Value of Equity (EVE) under SBP rate-shock scenarios (parallel and non-parallel +/-100/200/300 bps)
Establish one reconciled position store that feeds ALM, FTP, IFRS 9 ECL and Basel liquidity reporting from the same source of truth
pakistanDataSources: Sierra front-office (SYTRANS, SYENTITY, IXINST_DEF/MKM/EVT) for PIB, T-Bill and FX Forward positions, keyed by Trans_Num and Trade_Group (HMLB/HTMB/ASLB/ASMB)
Symbols / CBS retail (RB_ACCT, RB_TDA, RB_INT_DETAIL) for CASA and term deposits; CBS-CL (tm_ft_cl_loanbook, CL_DRAWDOWN) for the loan book

FIS ALM Physical Data Model targets: FixedInstruments, FloatingInstruments, NonMaturingInstruments, FXForwards plus Amortization/Coupon/EarlyTermination/Redemption cashflow tables (~260 standardized attributes)
GL reclass mapping (RB_GL_RECLASS, MPR_LINE, FSD_DOM_MAP_MASTER) to tag every position to its ledger account and asset/liability side
KIBOR / PKRV yield curves and INTEREST_RATE_INDEX reference rates for repricing and discounting
expectedOutcomes: ALCO-ready repricing and liquidity gap reports by bucket, currency and business line
NII-at-risk and EVE sensitivity under regulator-defined rate shocks, refreshed every run date
~260 standardized instrument attributes populated per position, replacing spreadsheet-based ALM
One golden position feed reused by ALM, FTP and IFRS 9, cutting reconciliation effort and breaks
keyChallenges: Several engine inputs (FTP_AverageBalance, FTP_AverageYield) do not exist in source and must be derived by the engine or pre-computed
LedgerAccount / GL tagging for many products is still 'to be confirmed by Finance' and depends on RB_GL_RECLASS and MPR_LINE lookups
The fixed-vs-floating flag (DirForDateGeneration) is derived case-by-case from CL_DRAWDOWN.FIXED_INT_RATE and Purpose codes, not stored directly
Islamic (Ameen) products need profit-rate treatment parallel to conventional interest, and FCY contracts must be revalued at spot

pakistanObjectives: Assign a matched-maturity transfer rate to every asset (charge) and liability (credit) so business-line margin splits into credit spread, funding/liquidity cost and interest-rate risk
Move all interest-rate and liquidity risk from the branches to the central Treasury book, leaving business units with a clean, risk-neutral customer spread
Populate the FIS engine FTP fields per instrument: FTP_RateCurveName, FTP_Coupon_Rate, FTP_Funding_Spread, FTP_Liquidity_Spread, FTP_Credit_Spread, FTP_Option_Spread and FTP_Margin
Attribute a defensible, auditable FTP result to each deal to drive risk-adjusted product pricing and RAROC
pakistanDataSources: Position feed from ALM (FixedInstruments / FloatingInstruments / NonMaturingInstruments) providing tenor, repricing and cashflow profile per deal
KIBOR / PKRV term structure as the FTP base curve (FTP_RateCurveName), with tenor-based liquidity-spread add-ons
Behavioral inputs for non-maturing deposits (FTP_AverageBalance, FTP_AverageYield, FTP_DeliveryType), which are not held in CBS source
Instrument optionality (prepayment, early termination, callable flags) for the option-cost component (FTP_Option_Spread)
expectedOutcomes: Per-deal, per-product and per-branch FTP-adjusted net interest margin
Transparent separation of who earns the spread (business) versus who owns the risk (Treasury)
Direct feed into the Customer Profitability Engine for FTP-adjusted EVA
Consistent transfer pricing across the conventional and Islamic books
keyChallenges: FTP inputs for savings/CASA (average balance, average yield, delivery type) are absent in Symbols and must be modeled behaviorally
Coupon payment frequency/anchor conventions for savings and Islamic products are undefined in source (open items in the mapping)
Requires an agreed FTP methodology and curve governance, which few Pakistan banks have formalized
Multi-currency deals need per-currency curves and consistent spot conversion

pakistanObjectives: Generate contractual and behavioral cashflows for every instrument from its principal, coupon, amortization, redemption and early-termination schedules
Model the four cashflow tables from source: AmortizationTable (principal), CouponCashflowTable (interest/profit), RedemptionTable and EarlyTerminationTable
Derive coupon and repricing dates from source event tables (IXINST_EVT/DEF for Sierra; CL_DRAWDOWN roll/interest dates for CBS loans)
Produce a dated cashflow ladder per position as the raw material for liquidity gap, NII and valuation
pakistanDataSources: Sierra IXINST_EVT / IXINST_DEF coupon and event schedules; GLTRDAMORT amortization; SYCLTRANS early-termination transactions
CBS-CL CL_DRAWDOWN (PRI_REPAY_FREQ, INT_REP_FREQ, ROLL_DATE, NEXT_INT_REP_DATE) and CL_REPAY / CL_PAID_INVOICE for repayments
RB_TDA / RB_TDA_PRETERM for term-deposit maturities and pre-termination amounts
FM_PERIOD_FREQ lookup to translate source frequency codes into the engine payment-frequency enums
expectedOutcomes: Complete principal + interest cashflow schedule per instrument, including grace periods and stubs
Behavioral overlays for prepayment (loans) and early withdrawal (deposits)
Reusable cashflow store feeding Liquidity, IRRBB and IFRS 9 effective-interest-rate calculations
Automation of schedules previously rebuilt manually for every ALM run
keyChallenges: Coupon/amortization payment amounts (Amort_PaymentAmount, coupon dates) are frequently 'Not Required / N-R' in source and must be engine-generated
Repayment frequency and repricing dates are spread across CL_DRAWDOWN fields and require FM_PERIOD_FREQ conversion
Islamic profit distribution and savings payout conventions are not yet defined in source
Holiday calendars and business-day conventions must be standardized across systems

pakistanObjectives: Build the structural liquidity (maturity) gap ladder from instrument cashflows across contractual and behavioral time buckets
Model non-maturing deposit (CASA) stability and run-off to separate core versus volatile balances
Compute Basel III LCR and NSFR and SBP liquidity metrics from the same position and cashflow feed
Stress liquidity under name-specific and market-wide scenarios (deposit flight, rollover failure)
pakistanDataSources: NonMaturingInstruments feed from CBS (RB_ACCT LEDGER_BAL, RB_GL_RECLASS) for CASA balances and GL classification
Cashflow ladder from Cashflow Generation (amortization, coupon, redemption, early-termination)
Term-deposit maturities (RB_TDA MATURITY_DATE) and pre-termination behavior (RB_TDA_PRETERM)
HQLA inventory from the Sierra securities book (PIB/T-Bill AFS/HFT) with market values and haircuts
expectedOutcomes: Daily maturity-ladder and cumulative gap by bucket and currency
Core-versus-volatile deposit split with behavioral run-off assumptions
LCR / NSFR ratios and early-warning liquidity indicators for ALCO
Contingency-funding insight linking the HQLA buffer to stressed outflows
keyChallenges: Behavioral maturity of CASA is not in source and needs a decay/stability model per product and segment
Deposit average-balance inputs (FTP_AverageBalance) are missing and must be derived
FCY liquidity needs per-currency ladders and spot revaluation
Early-termination / preterm penalties (PRETERM_AMT net of interest, WHT and Zakat) complicate outflow timing

pakistanObjectives: Produce the repricing gap between rate-sensitive assets and liabilities per time bucket from each instrument repricing profile
Capture repricing attributes per position: Repricing_NextRepricingDate, Repricing_Freq, Repricing_RateCurveName, Repricing_Margin and Repricing_Cap/Floor
Quantify IRRBB via EVE and NII sensitivity under SBP-prescribed parallel and non-parallel rate shocks
Distinguish fixed versus floating exposure and index basis (KIBOR tenor) to manage basis and repricing risk
pakistanDataSources: Floating instrument repricing from CL_DRAWDOWN (ROLL_DATE = next repricing; ROLL_DATE - INT_FREQ = last repricing) and RB_INT_DETAIL spreads
Fixed-vs-floating determination from CL_DRAWDOWN.FIXED_INT_RATE and Sierra Purpose codes (TFCV/PIBF)
INTEREST_RATE_INDEX reference curves (KIBOR 1M/3M/6M/1Y) and spread/margin per deal
Instrument caps, floors and rate multipliers from the FIS repricing attribute set
expectedOutcomes: Rate-sensitivity (repricing) gap ladder and duration measures for ALCO
EVE and NII-at-risk under +/-100/200/300 bps shocks
Basis-risk view across KIBOR tenors and the fixed/floating mix
Inputs to hedging decisions (interest-rate swaps) and FTP curve construction
keyChallenges: Repricing dates are derived, not stored: ROLL_DATE arithmetic and FM_PERIOD_FREQ conversion are required
Threshold / split / tiered rates (RB-OD, rate schemes) need correct effective-rate selection logic
Behavioral repricing of administered savings rates differs from contractual and must be modeled
Cap/floor optionality needs volatility inputs (FTP_*_VolaAtOrigin) not present in source

pakistanObjectives: Classify securities by accounting intent HTM / AFS / HFT (Sierra Trade_Group and Purpose codes) to drive amortized-cost versus fair-value measurement
Capture MarketValue (clean/dirty), BookValue and amortized cost per position from IXINST_MKM prices and GLTRDAMORT
Support fair-value and hedge-accounting entries and AFS reserve movements
Reconcile position book values to the GL via ledger tagging
pakistanDataSources: Sierra IXINST_MKM (MID_PRICE, MID_YTM) mark-to-market and IXINST_DEF instrument definitions
GLTRDAMORT amortized cost / book value by Trade_Group and amort date (Sysdate-1)
Trade_Group / Purpose classification (HMLB/HTMB, ASLB/ASMB AFS, TBILL, PIB) for accounting category
FSD_DOM_MAP_MASTER and MPR_LINE for GL / ledger-account mapping
expectedOutcomes: Correct measurement basis per security (amortized cost versus FVOCI versus FVTPL)
Daily clean/dirty market value and unrealized gain/loss for the AFS reserve
Auditable link from instrument to accounting category and ledger
Consistent valuation feed shared with ALM and market-risk
keyChallenges: MarketValue price basis (clean versus dirty, price versus yield) must be standardized from IXINST_MKM
Book value depends on GLTRDAMORT amort-date alignment and Trans_Num joins
Reclassification between HTM/AFS/HFT changes measurement and must be tracked
GL / ledger mapping for several instruments is still pending Finance confirmation

pakistanObjectives: Stage every exposure (IFRS 9 Stage 1/2/3) using CD_CreditQualityStage, CD_DaysPastDueStage and loan-performance status carried on the ALM feed
Attach risk parameters per position: PD_12M (point-in-time and through-the-cycle), PD_Lifetime, LGD and CreditConversionFactor
Compute Expected Credit Loss and LossAllowance on the same instrument-level cashflows used for ALM (effective-interest-rate discounting)
Align ECL provisioning with SBP requirements and Basel asset classes
pakistanDataSources: ALM position feed carrying CD_* dimensions (CreditQualityStage, DaysPastDueStage, Rating, Segment, Product) and TotalPastDueAmount
CBS loan book (tm_ft_cl_loanbook, CL_DRAWDOWN) status flags and past-due buckets; RB_OD_REPOSITORY for retail overdrafts
PD/LGD models (PROBABILITY_OF_DEFAULT_MODEL, LOSS_GIVEN_DEFAULT_RISK_GRADE_VALUE) and Basel parameters
Contractual + behavioral cashflows from Cashflow Generation for lifetime-ECL discounting
expectedOutcomes: Stage-wise ECL (12-month and lifetime) and loss allowance per exposure and portfolio
Provision coverage aligned to SBP and IFRS 9, reconciled to GL (PROVISION_FOR_LOAN_LOSS_ACCOUNT)
Consistent PD/LGD parameters shared with Basel RWA and risk-based pricing
Early-warning staging driven by days-past-due and rating migration
keyChallenges: Past-due numbers are applied at loan-number level and must be spread to drawdown/position level
Dual conventional/Islamic books and multiple CBS sources complicate a single exposure view
PIT-versus-TTC PD calibration and macro-scenario weighting require model governance
SICR staging thresholds need agreed, auditable rules across products
